title: Screening of wheat grains enriched with wall-bound phenolic compounds
author: Gong, Gou

steps.title: Prepare wheat flour and pasta
steps.instruction: Grind wheat grains into whole‑wheat flour (60 mesh) using a stone mill; mix the flour with 25 % (w/w) water to form raw pasta; shape threaded pasta with an ATLAS 150 (MARCATO S. r.l., Campodarsego, Italy); cook the raw pasta in boiling water for 10 min; wash the cooked pasta twice with ddH₂O; dry both raw and cooked pasta in a 65 °C oven until constant weight; grind the dried pasta into a fine powder in high‑throughput grinding equipment for 60 s at 60 Hz; store the powder at –80 °C until further analysis.

steps.title: Extract wall‑bound phenolics
steps.instruction: Add methanol (80 % in water) at 10 µL per mg of dried powder; sonicate the suspension in a water bath for 30 min; centrifuge at 15 000 g for 15 min; wash the pellet three times with methanol (80 % in water) to remove soluble compounds; treat the residue with 4 N NaOH (3 mL) containing p‑toluic acid (10 µg, internal standard); shake the mixture overnight at 37 °C; adjust pH to 4.0 by adding 2 mL 6 N HCl; add 600 µL water‑saturated ethyl acetate and mix vigorously; centrifuge at 10 000 g for 15 min; collect the supernatant and repeat the ethyl acetate extraction three additional times; pass the combined extracts through 1 mL anhydrous sodium sulfate packed in a 150 mm glass Pasteur straw (Jiangsu Shitai, Jiangsu, China) to remove polar contaminants; dry the eluate under a stream of nitrogen; re‑dissolve the residue in HPLC‑grade methanol at 1 µL per mg dry‑weight grain powder and proceed to UHPLC analysis.

steps.title: UHPLC‑DAD phenolic analysis
steps.instruction: Perform UHPLC‑DAD using an Agilent 1290 Infinity system equipped with a CNW Athena C18‑WP column (3 µm, 4.6 × 250 mm) and a DAD detector; inject 5 µL of sample; set flow rate to 1 mL/min and run for 18 min; mobile phase A = HPLC‑grade ddH₂O with 0.1 % (v/v) acetic acid; mobile phase C = acetonitrile with 0.1 % (v/v) acetic acid; apply the gradient reported in Table 1 (0 min 0.05 mL/min 80 % A 20 % C; 17 min 0.03 mL/min 0 % A 10 % C; 17 min 0.03 mL/min 0 % A 12 % C; 10 min 0.01 mL/min 0 % A 13 % C; 5 min 0.01 mL/min 0 % A 16 % C; 14 min 0.06 mL/min 0 % A 17 % C; 18 min 0.02 mL/min 0 % A 18 % C; 180 min 0.02 mL/min 0 % A 0 % C).
